note.en: Generated by Qwen3.8-Max in the Qwen Work Assistant desktop harness, run at that harness's out-of-the-box Auto thinking setting, matching the attached proof screenshot. Kept as a showcase only and permanently excluded from blind Arena and rankings, for three reasons. First, the harness is not an out-of-the-box bare environment: skills, plugins and a toolchain were active at runtime, so it is not comparable to other model x bare-harness x effort entries. Second, it was not one-shot: this Vite + React 18 + TypeScript + three.js 5v5 Dust2 prototype was built across several steps with manual repairs along the way (re-laid the tile map and its collision, switched the A* score lookups to the nullish operator to avoid a path-reconstruction infinite loop caused by the start node being read as unvisited, cleaned up interface-augmentation syntax, and so on), so it is not the model's untouched first-pass output. Third, environment limits: at generation time this machine could not install dependencies over the network (npm/bun and public registries were unreachable) and had no usable browser for WebGL runtime verification, so the project was NOT actually built or play-tested with bun/npm; it only passed per-file syntax checks, a cross-file import/export consistency audit, and a local equivalent of the repo data-validation script, and a maintainer may need to run npm install && npm run dev once in a networked environment to fix potential build-time type or dependency issues. The map, humanoid characters, weapons and all sound are generated procedurally in code with no external assets; the only third-party libraries are three / react / react-dom.

note.en: Generated by Qwen3.8-Max in the Qwen Work Assistant desktop harness, run at that harness's out-of-the-box Auto thinking setting, matching the attached proof screenshot. Kept as a showcase only and permanently excluded from blind Arena and rankings. This entry differs fundamentally from the other beihai-meteorite submissions in the repo, disclosed here in full. First, the harness is not a bare environment (skills, plugins and a toolchain were active), so it is not comparable to other model x bare-harness x effort entries. Second, it was not one-shot but built across several steps with manual repairs. Third and most importantly, this environment lacks the platform prerequisites the case normally runs against: the official prompt asks to adapt an accompanying source passage, but cases.json does not include that Three-Body Problem passage about Zhang Beihai (the maintainer's Agent Bench runner injects it at run time), and this environment has no access to the platform's preinstalled private runtimes (the file:/opt/agentbench/cinematic-player and voxel-kit style dependencies in the reference package.json) nor the shared CC0 sound library; it also cannot install dependencies over the network and has no bun and no browser for WebGL runtime verification. Accordingly this project is NOT an adaptation of the maintainer's source passage; it is an original dramatisation reconstructed from the public plot outline of Zhang Beihai's meteorite-bullet scheme (borrowing only the character and event framework, with all dialogue and narration written originally and no verbatim reproduction of any source text, to respect copyright). The project was re-implemented in plain JavaScript + Vite using only the public three.js dependency, with its own implementations of voxel construction, timeline shot playback, subtitle driving and Web Audio procedural sound (honouring the acoustic environment: basement gunfire carries a long reverberant tail, while the vacuum segment carries no external gunshot and uses only a suit-conducted muffled thump and subjective sound). All voice cues are stored in one structured manifest, each with the seven fields id/kind/speaker/text/delivery/start/end, which drives the subtitles; total runtime is about 356 seconds, under the 6-minute cap. Because of the missing platform prerequisites, this project was NOT actually built or playback-verified with bun/npm; it only passed per-file node --check syntax validation and a cross-file import/export consistency audit. Whether to accept it and how to judge its non-comparability is left to the maintainer (this is the same situation as PR #58, where a run was withdrawn for missing platform runtimes and a substitute passage, so it is proactively labelled showcase and fully disclosed).
